source_title: Hayden Panettiere Leads Emotional 2026 Daytime Emmys In Memoriam Tribute - People.com
source_excerpt:
The 53rd annual Daytime Emmy Awards ‘In Memoriam’ began with a special tribute to Eric Bauza, who died on Sunday, Oct. 25
Julia Moore is a TV Writer-Reporter at PEOPLE. She has been working at PEOPLE since 2022.
The 53rd annual Daytime Emmy Awards honored those who have died this year during the “In Memoriam” tribute
This included stars Hayden Panettiere, Anthony Geary, Robert Kelker-Kelly, Eric Bauza and more
The awards ceremony was held in Los Angeles on Friday, Oct. 30
The soap world remembered some of its brightest stars at the 2026 Daytime Emmys.
During the 53rd annual ceremony on Friday, Oct. 30, the television community honored Eric Bauza , Hayden Panettiere , Robert Kelker-Kelly and Anthony Geary and others who died in the past year.
The “In Memoriam” segment opened with a tribute to Bauza, a Looney Tunes voice actor famous for voicing Bugs Bunny and Daffy Duck. Bauza died of hypertensive cardiovascular disease on Sunday, Oct. 25, at age 46.
“So many of us in this room were shocked and saddened this week to learn of the passing of a good friend of this Academy. If I mention the name Eric Bauza, some people might not recognize it immediately, but if you heard his voice, or should I say his many voices, you would most certainly recognize him and appreciate the remarkable contribution that he made to our industry,” the presenter said.
“Bugs Bunny, Daffy Duck, Porky Pig, Tweety, Marvin the Martian, the characters that the legendary Mel Blank made famous, living on through Eric’s remarkable talent,” he continued. “Bugs Bunny actually received his first Emmy recognition courtesy of Eric back in 2022 because Eric won an outstanding voice performance award for a Looney Tunes production that included the rascally rabbit.”
Throughout his career, Bauza earned five Emmy nominations, winning three.
Panettiere, known for her roles on hit TV series Nashville and Heroes , was also honored during the ceremony’s “In Memoriam” segment. The actress — who got her start as a child star on soaps like Guiding Light and One Life to Live — died at age 36 on Aug. 16 after being found unresponsive at an Airbnb in Greenville, S.C.
Her death was ruled accidental by the Greenville County Coroner’s Office on Sept. 22, with officials citing the toxic effects of multiple drugs, including fentanyl. Earlier this week, the Greenville Police Department confirmed to PEOPLE that her death was accidental and that its investigation had concluded.
“She was an incredible light and a force of nature who brought immeasurable love and joy to all who knew her — and to the millions who watched her onscreen,” the actress’ rep said in a statement to PEOPLE.
Geary, who starred in General Hospital as Luke Spencer, died on Dec. 14, at age 78. The actor’s death came after he experienced complications from an operation three days prior.
“It was a shock for me and our families and our friends,” Geary’s husband, Claudio Gama, told the outlet in a statement. “For more than 30 years, Tony has been my friend, my companion, my husband.”
Geary originated the role of Luke on the soap opera in 1978. Luke was ultimately paired with Genie Francis’s Laura, and together they became daytime’s biggest supercouple .
Days of our Lives star Robert Kelker-Kelly was among those recognized during the in memoriam. He died on Oct. 3 at 62 of arteriosclerotic heart disease .
He experienced alarming symptoms, including chest and arm pain, prior to his death , according to a police report obtained by PEOPLE. His wife Allison Kelly told authorities that she picked up her husband, a professional pilot, from Spirit Airport at approximately 7:30 p.m. that evening. While driving home, Kelker-Kelly complained of pain in his left arm and chest.
At this year’s awards show, The Young and the Restless led with 18 nominations, with newcomer Beyond the Gates following closely behind with 16 nominations. General Hospital earned 13 nominations and Days of Our Lives eight.
The 2026 Daytime Emmy Awards are streaming live on YouTube.
